key_insight: A hybrid nanocone-plus-nanohole silicon texture improves thin-film solar absorption by reducing front reflection and boosting internal light trapping.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a practical route to higher-efficiency thin-film silicon cells while maintaining strong thermal robustness under operating conditions.
method: Front-surface silicon nanocones create a gradual refractive-index transition to suppress reflection.
Embedded air-filled nanoholes increase optical confinement via scattering and internal reflection.
FDTD optical simulation was coupled with electrical and opto-electro-thermal device modeling to optimize geometry and doping.
evidence_signal: The optimized device reached 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% FF, and 24.42% efficiency, retaining 95.21% efficiency up to 45°C.
watch_item: The reported gains depend on precise nanoscale patterning and integrated thermal performance, so fabrication tolerance and manufacturability remain key concerns.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
